dedupe_keys.name: report on outages and curtailments during the southwest cold weather event of february 1 5 2011 ferc and nerc staff august 2011

description: This case study is the joint FERC and NERC staff report on the outages and gas curtailments during the Southwest cold weather event of 1 to 5 February 2011, published in August 2011 in 357 pages. It has chapters on the electric and natural gas industries, preparations for the storm, load shed and curtailments, causes of the outages and supply disruptions, prior cold weather events, electric and gas interdependencies, and key findings and recommendations. The executive summary reports that 67 percent of generator failures by MWh were directly due to weather, that 14.8 Bcf of gas production was lost, and that more than 50,000 gas customers were curtailed, with nearly half of ERCOT's black start units unavailable. Access: free PDF from the FERC website; no licence is stated. Coverage is Texas, New Mexico and Arizona in 2011, ten years before Winter Storm Uri. Caveats: only the contents and executive summary pages were read here. It suits cascading failure and resilience studies of coupled electricity and gas systems in cold weather, and no directly related records are catalogued yet.

name: Report on Outages and Curtailments During the Southwest Cold Weather Event of February 1-5, 2011 (FERC and NERC staff, August 2011)
outcomes: Weather caused generator trips, derates and failures to start across the Southwest; for the region 67 percent of generator failures by MWh were directly weather-related and at least another 12 percent indirect, load shedding included 1,023 MW at El Paso Electric and 300 MW at Salt River Project, and ERCOT spot prices hit the 3,000 dollars per MWh cap on 2 February. An estimated 14.8 Bcf of gas production was lost, from freeze-offs, icy roads and blackouts, leading to gas curtailments to more than 50,000 customers in New Mexico, Arizona and Texas. The report closes with key findings and recommendations on winterization, black start units, load shedding training and electric and gas interdependencies.
